notes: `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` section 10.1, Task 6: verify `T = T↑` under the views `Vb = G ⋈ E` and `Ve = E ⋈ G`. Global schema `{E, G}` with `E` the digraph edge relation and the unary `G` marking the "good" vertices; local schema `{Vb, Ve}` with the exact conjunctive views `Vb(x, y) ↔ G(x) ∧ E(x, y)` and `Ve(x, y) ↔ E(x, y) ∧ G(y)`.

The source documents the reformulations task document (sha256 `32a3ac6b428d851f0aaa4fb7acdbf2fe4ad5dacca93ee118837888ff91b7a1c6`) and `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` (sha256 `796ff97c082c6fc70e75a60c0dd40ec0680b738d7184a8b8aefea8c681b3ebff`) carry the same section 10.1 text, so both name this task.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example4035.lean` states the PDF's Datalog programs, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the two compiled commands one after the other, renames the generated snapshots `T_1` and `TUp_1` to the auxiliary input names `T_aux` and `TUp_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` as the pair of view equations and `inputPost` as the claim `T = TUp` and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence.

Expected verdict valid. Substituting the view definitions turns each `TUp` rule into the matching `T` rule, so the two least fixpoints coincide. The classification stays `unknown` because this corpus carries no certificate.

title: Good-interior path query versus its begin-good and end-good edge-view reformulation
explanation: The global program T computes walks of length at least two through digraph E whose interior vertices are all "good" (marked by unary relation G): T(x,y):-E(x,z),G(z),E(z,y), and T(x,y):-E(x,z),G(z),T(z,y) — a good-interior-vertex reachability query. The local reformulation TUp is defined over two exact conjunctive views, Vb (begin-good edges, G(x) ∧ E(x,y)) and Ve (end-good edges, E(x,y) ∧ G(y)): TUp(x,y):-Ve(x,z),Vb(z,y), and TUp(x,y):-Ve(x,z),TUp(z,y). The Hoare triple claims the two programs compute the same relation, T = TUp — an equivalence claim that follows from substituting the view definitions into each TUp rule to recover the matching T rule. Expected valid; no certificate exists yet, so the classification stays unknown.
preInWords: The precondition states the two view equations exactly: Vb is the join of G and E giving good-start edges, and Ve is the join of E and G giving good-end edges.
postInWords: The postcondition asserts T = TUp, that the good-interior path query and its two-view reformulation agree.
